ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the small figure on the left, there is a section of continental coast; the land is represented by shading on the left, and the right side is labeled as ocean; the nearshore position is marked “A.” There are two isotherms in the ocean; the isotherm labeled 25℃ is located relatively above, the isotherm labeled 21℃ is located relatively below, and the isotherms bend near A. The right side is a world map, marked with four positions: Jia, Yi, Bing, and Ding. Then reason: in the left figure, 25℃ is above and 21℃ is below, indicating that the farther downward, the lower the temperature, so it can be judged that this sea area is located in the Southern Hemisphere. The land is on the left and the ocean on the right, so A is located offshore of the east coast of a continent; combined with the bending of the isotherms, A can be determined to be a warm current on the east coast of a Southern Hemisphere continent. In the world map on the right, among the four marked positions, the one that conforms to the distribution of a “warm current on the east coast of a Southern Hemisphere continent” is Ding. Therefore ocean current A might appear at Ding.
